# Design tokens

**Generated from `tokens/tokens.json` by `npm run tokens`. Do not edit this file.**
To change a value, edit `tokens/tokens.json` and regenerate. The other generated
view is `build/css/tokens.css`, which is what the app actually consumes.

The `Resolves to` column follows every `{reference}` chain down to the raw value,
so a semantic token shows the literal it ends at as well as the primitive it points
through.

## Colour semantics

`color.semantic.*` — 93 tokens

Roles. These are what components bind to.

| Token | Value | Resolves to | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color.semantic.background.page` | `{color.primitive.navy.950}` | `#090C18` | Root screen canvas. Use for every screen's base background; not for cards, sheets, or modals. |
| `color.semantic.background.surface` | `{color.primitive.navy.800}` | `#22242F` | Elevated container fill. Use for cards, bottom sheets, modals, dropdown menus, chat bubbles, toasts. |
| `color.semantic.background.raised` | `{color.primitive.alpha.light-06}` | `#FFFFFF0F` | A surface sitting on top of another surface. Use when a card or row needs to separate from a container that is itself background.surface — the confirmed case is an optionRow inside a bottomSheet, where both would otherwise resolve to the same value and the row would vanish. Translucent on purpose so it composites correctly over any surface beneath it. Not a replacement for background.surface; only reach for it when there is a genuine second layer. |
| `color.semantic.background.inverse` | `{color.primitive.violet.50}` | `#F4F2FF` | Light fill for dark surfaces. Confirmed live use is status bar icon glyphs only; other uses unconfirmed. |
| `color.semantic.background.scrim` | `{color.primitive.alpha.dark-50}` | `#0A0A0A80` | Semi-transparent overlay dimming content behind a modal. |
| `color.semantic.background.floating` | `{color.primitive.alpha.glass-60}` | `#3D3D3D99` | Elevated floating surface with translucency, for dropdowns, tooltips, popovers. |
| `color.semantic.background.stacking` | `{color.primitive.alpha.light-10}` | `#FFFFFF1A` | Additive white layer for stacking elevation on dark surfaces, e.g. toasts. RISK: resolves to the same value as interactive.secondary, interactive.disabled and interactive.pressed — coincidental, this token is a static elevation layer, not an interaction state, so the overlap is lower-risk here than for the other three. |
| `color.semantic.background.input` | `{color.primitive.navy.900}` | `#1A1C26` | Fill of an editable field at rest; use text.primary for filled text, text.disabled for placeholders. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.primary` | `{color.primitive.violet.50}` | `#F4F2FF` | Main call-to-action fill. Max one interactive.primary button per screen. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.primary:hover` | `{color.primitive.violet.100}` | `#E4E0FF` | Hover state of interactive.primary, primary buttons only. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.primary:active` | `{color.primitive.violet.200}` | `#D2CCFA` | Pressed state of interactive.primary, primary buttons only. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.secondary` | `{color.primitive.alpha.light-10}` | `#FFFFFF1A` | Supporting action fill: Skip, Cancel, filter chips, outlined buttons, toggles. RISK: resolves to the same value as interactive.disabled, background.stacking and interactive.pressed. Secondary and disabled are intentionally meant to read as equally quiet/receding — but if a secondary and a disabled control ever sit next to each other in the same view, a student has no color cue to tell them apart. Check that context before assuming this token alone carries the distinction. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.secondary:hover` | `{color.primitive.alpha.light-18}` | `#FFFFFF2E` | Hover state of interactive.secondary. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.secondary:active` | `{color.primitive.alpha.light-24}` | `#FFFFFF3D` | Pressed state of interactive.secondary. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.destructive` | `{color.primitive.red.400}` | `#FF6B6B` | Irreversible harmful action fill: delete, remove, block buttons. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.destructive:hover` | `{color.primitive.red.300}` | `#FF8585` | Hover state of interactive.destructive. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.destructive:active` | `{color.primitive.red.500}` | `#E85555` | Pressed state of interactive.destructive. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.disabled` | `{color.primitive.alpha.light-10}` | `#FFFFFF1A` | Non-interactive control fill signaling unavailable. RISK: resolves to the same value as interactive.secondary, background.stacking and interactive.pressed. For this feature specifically: a mic button disabled by denied permission must not be visually confusable with an ordinary secondary button — pair this with text.disabled and consider whether disabled state needs a non-color signal (icon change, label) as well. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.onDisabled` | `{color.primitive.alpha.light-40}` | `#FFFFFF66` | Text and icons on interactive.disabled fills. Alias of text.disabled's value, kept in the interactive family so disabled controls (buttons, mic) don't reach into the text.* family for their icon/label color. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.onPrimary` | `{color.primitive.navy.950}` | `#090C18` | Text and icons on interactive.primary fills; must contrast >= 4.5:1. Aliases navy.950 (16.6:1 on interactive.primary). Corrected 2026-09-16: this file said homie.inkwell (3.1:1), Figma has always said navy.950; Figma wins. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.onSecondary` | `{color.primitive.violet.50}` | `#F4F2FF` | Text and icons on interactive.secondary fills. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.onDestructive` | `{color.primitive.red.950}` | `#2A0808` | Text and icons on interactive.destructive fills; must contrast >= 4.5:1. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.pressed` | `{color.primitive.alpha.light-10}` | `#FFFFFF1A` | Semi-transparent tap-feedback overlay for light or vivid surfaces, when no dedicated :active token exists. Applied on top of the resting fill, never as a standalone background. RISK: of the four tokens sharing this value, this is the one most likely to need independent tuning later — it's a transient tap overlay, not a static surface. If contrast ever needs adjusting for it alone, split it into its own primitive rather than nudging alpha.light-10 and affecting the other three. |
| `color.semantic.interactive.pressedInverse` | `{color.primitive.alpha.dark-10}` | `#0A0A0A1A` | Semi-transparent tap-feedback overlay for dark surfaces, when no dedicated :active token exists. |

| `color.semantic.text.secondary` | `{color.primitive.alpha.light-68}` | `#F5F3FFAD` | Reduced emphasis text: subtitles, captions, timestamps, helper text. |
| `color.semantic.text.tertiary` | `{color.primitive.alpha.light-52}` | `#FFFFFF85` | Lowest emphasis readable text: timestamps, counts, inline hints, eyebrow labels (hintCard "Hint", recallResult "You said"); not for anything a student must read to proceed. ## Component tokens

`component.*` — 22 tokens

> Component tokens exist only when a component's bindings actually branch by state or variant in a way that benefits from its own indirection layer between it and the semantic tokens, not as documentation-only aliases for a value that never changes. micButton is the only entry here on purpose: its four states each pair with a different semantic token, and these tokens are the real thing its Figma variables are bound to, not a restatement of them. chatBubble and hintCard never branch, they bind straight to semantic tokens with nothing in between, so a component.chatBubble.* or component.hintCard.* entry here would just be a second name for a value already named once. optionRow does branch by state the same way micButton does, four variants, four different fills, but its Figma variants bind straight to the semantic tokens directly rather than through a component-specific layer. That's an inconsistency with micButton's pattern, not a mistake exactly, treat micButton's indirection layer as the older, legacy approach rather than the template: an indirection layer that never diverges from what it aliases is upkeep with no payoff. Don't add one to a new component by default. Add one only when there's a concrete reason a component's own token might need to move independently of the semantic token it currently matches.

| Token | Value | Resolves to | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `component.button.s.height` | `32` |  | Size S pill height. Inside a 48px tap target (spacing.semantic.tapTarget). |
| `component.button.m.height` | `40` |  | Size M pill height. Inside a 48px tap target (spacing.semantic.tapTarget). |
| `component.button.l.height` | `56` |  | Size L pill height. Taller than the tap target, so the pill is the hit area. |
| `component.scaffold.panelHeader.height` | `48` |  | Status-bar region at the top of every screen. A literal: 48 here is the iOS status-bar area, unrelated to size.primitive.space.1200 (a spacing step) or spacing.semantic.tapTarget (a hit-area floor, which its own description says is not a layout rhythm value). |
| `component.scaffold.topNavigation.height` | `56` |  | Region holding the appBar and the session fraction. A literal: component.button.l.height is also 56, but aliasing across components is how a value silently changes for the wrong reason. |
| `component.scaffold.bottomContent.height` | `120` |  | The action zone at the foot of a screen. A literal: size.primitive.illustration.1500 is also 120, but that is an illustration box and a footer region is not one. component.micButton.diameter does alias it, legitimately, because a micButton genuinely is a 120 illustration-sized circle. |
| `component.scaffold.bottomSheetOnly.height` | `34` |  | Home-indicator region, and the slot a bottom sheet occupies on its own branch screen. No primitive of this value exists. |

---

292 tokens across 10 groups.
